title: JSON vs JavaScript: Understanding the Difference
author: Reconnect Master
description: Clarifying the confusion between JSON and JavaScript—they're related but fundamentally different.
content: # JSON vs JavaScript: Understanding the Key Differences
Beginners often confuse JSON and JavaScript because JSON syntax looks familiar. But they serve different purposes.
- Handles events, manipulates data, controls behavior
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a **data format**:
- A standardized way to store and transport data
- Used by APIs, databases, configuration files
| **Execution** | Can execute functions | No execution, just data |
| **Quotes** | Strings can use single or double quotes | Strings MUST use double quotes |
| **Functions** | Can contain methods and functions | Cannot contain functions |
| **Undefined** | Can use undefined values | No undefined, only null |
| **Comments** | Supports comments // or /* */ | No comments allowed |
JSON is a **subset** of JavaScript syntax:
- Valid JSON is usually valid JavaScript
- But valid JavaScript might not be valid JSON
- In JavaScript, you can parse JSON: `JSON.parse(jsonString)`
- JSON lives inside JavaScript, not the other way around
